documents: Unaccompanied Personal Baggage Declaration (NZCS218 and NZCS218A)
MPI Personal Effects Supplementary Declaration, filled in when packing
Proof of right to live in NZ, e.g. residence or 12-month+ work visa
Prescription or doctor's letter for medicines
dutyFree: Used goods owned before you left, if you lived abroad for 21+ months
You must hold an eligible visa and goods must be for your own use
Cars owned and used 12+ months, if not sold within 24 months
restricted: Meat, honey, eggs, dairy, popcorn and most plant products are banned
Tobacco needs a Customs permit and is charged high duty and tax
Firearms need a NZ Police licence and import permit; pistols are banned
Garden tools, outdoor furniture and sports gear are checked for biosecurity
Mothballs containing naphthalene, camphor or dichlorobenzene are banned
notes: All shipments go through an approved facility; containers are not delivered to your door
Brand-new items must be declared and may attract duty and GST
Goods arriving over 5 years after you need Customs approval for duty-free entry
Wooden packaging must carry the ISPM 15 mark

documents: Copy of passport and visa page
Inventory, or list of boxes you packed yourself
Customs forms required by the destination country
List of any alcohol and electronic items
Signed service contract with your contact details
For a car: registration, purchase invoice and odometer reading
restricted: Batteries for e-bikes, e-scooters and hoverboards cannot be exported
Other batteries are only taken if the carrier and port agree
notes: No special export clearance for used goods or cars beyond these documents
Car owners must approve battery disconnection and fuel draining if needed
